resan-genom-sagoland.evidence: Original Swedish printed-on-board rules of Sago-Konst A.B., Stockholm, Resan genom Sagoland recovered from actual public Tradera gallery photographs. The distinctive 113-space board, twenty numbered fairy-tale event verses, title, publisher, included markers/spinner and die substitution match named BGG 93006. All four retained original photos were visually inspected: whole board, pocket close-up, front and back cover. The board bears E. Norelius 42; this is an artwork signature/date, not certification of the release year or all editions. The complete board and all twenty verse blocks are present in the unchanged full photograph, with no captioned modern replacement panel as in the earlier held BGG image. This is an original RULEBOOK IMAGES source in the form of printed board instructions, not a recovered separate booklet or publisher PDF. The two-page PDF is explicitly a local convenience assembly of the unchanged whole-board and pocket photographs. Four unchanged JPEGs plus the actual linking HTML are retained with actual offered URLs, dimensions and SHA-256 hashes. Only the first original-resolution URL is offered by the gallery og:image; other photos use actually offered large-fit URLs. No CDN signatures or higher-resolution addresses were invented. Fresh Swedish OCR was attempted on analysis-only rotated/perspective-adjusted board regions and the close-up, but produced many wrong words and numbers. It is not certified as a full transcription. Canonical text instead gives explicitly labelled manually read Swedish excerpts from the clear event instructions and pocket; decorative verse wording and the blurry first event are not reconstructed. Original photographs govern. The source supplies concrete forward/backward moves, missed throws, extra throws, return to zero, remaining until last, player removal at 59 and the final gold-chest verse at 113. It does not establish the summary’s youngest-player start, solo/age/player-count claims, optional tokens, exact-landing requirement, spinner distribution or every chaining/elimination edge case. No missing general rules are invented. The original spinner and markers are not separately recovered; a playable printable component set is not certified. Finnish aliases and museum searches were discovery leads only; no memoir was substituted as rules. No full summary audit, PASS, body repair or verified badge.

fury-in-the-west.evidence: Publisher Avalon Hill The General, volume 18 number 1, May-June 1981, Robert D. Harmon, Fury in the West: A Commander’s Notebook. Actual unchanged 50-page magazine PDF retrieved successfully. Cover date/issue native text and original printed page 3 title/byline/publisher preface identify it. The preface explicitly says the Battleline game needed no Avalon Hill revision beyond new map and bookcase packaging, supporting the named Battleline 1977 game rather than a different title. Original images of printed/PDF pages 3, 6, 7 and 9 were visually read. Canonical selected regions contain the publisher preface, full Critical Issue 1 Initial Briefing, Critical Issue 2 Unit Reduction and Critical Issue 3 Rules, ending before Critical Issue 4 Union Organization. Coverage includes brigade forces and leader chains, three scenarios/day-night structure, offboard permanent casualty and recoverable straggler tracks, examples, ordinary movement attrition, columns, elimination when tracks meet, flank/rear doubling, two units per hex, frontal-three-hex ZOC/mandatory combat/withdrawal, facing costs, advanced artillery/night/reorganization, explicitly optional initiative/cavalry/stacking/leader/other variants, and scenario-specific victory points. Normal day-one Confederate/day-two Union initiative is distinct from the optional die-roll initiative rule. Day-one Pittsburgh Landing and day-two Shiloh Church bonuses are distinguished from the two-day scenario, which lacks special territorial objectives. This is an accurately labelled publisher-magazine RULES REFERENCE PDF, not the complete original rulebook. Exact scenario starting hexes, full terrain/movement costs, complete CRT, strength records, all recovery rates/edge cases and original physical components remain missing. Native text has old OCR spelling/hyphenation artifacts; source page images govern exact wording and numbers. Regions preserve original column order and stop before unrelated organization/strategy sections. The later author-proposed alternative setups, victory conditions and new optional rules on pages 12–13 are excluded. Printed Optional Rules on page 9 remain explicitly optional, including recommendations/commentary. The earlier volume18number5 PDF has only a product advertisement and is held, not accepted as the rules feature. Grognard’s user-inferred leader elimination erratum is not promoted into official rules. One specific source-backed MAJOR finding records omitted mandatory ordinary-movement straggler losses; no full summary audit, PASS or body repair.
fury-in-the-west.specific_finding: The summary describes stragglers as accumulating from continuous combat and omits mandatory losses from ordinary movement. The publisher rules discussion in Avalon Hill The General 18-1, May-June 1981, printed page 7, explicitly says each unit loses one SFP whether it moves one hex or four, with examples of one SFP lost per turn of movement even without casualties. Stationary units can recover stragglers, and the Advanced Game column formation is an explicit movement exception. Casualty and straggler markers meeting eliminates the unit. Omitting ordinary movement attrition changes maneuver, resting decisions and whether a brigade survives. Specific MAJOR finding only; no full rulebook audit or summary-body repair.
